tour.name: Kilimanjaro Private Day Hike to Mandara Hut & Materuni Waterfalls with Chagga Coffee
tour.subtitle: A taste of Africa's highest mountain in a private day with a licensed mountain guide: a hike through the rainforest on the Marangu route to Mandara Hut and the Maundi Crater, then the Materuni waterfall in the foothills and a coffee experience with a Chagga family.

highlights: A hike on Kilimanjaro, the highest mountain in Africa
The montane rainforest with colobus monkeys
The view from the Maundi Crater towards the summit
The Materuni waterfall in the foothills
Roasting and grinding coffee with a Chagga family
tour.overview:
Mount Kilimanjaro, at 5,895 metres, is the highest mountain in Africa and the highest freestanding mountain in the world. Climbing to its summit takes at least five days, but its lower slopes, covered in rainforest, can be explored in a day. The Chagga people, who live on its fertile foothills, grow bananas and some of Tanzania's finest coffee.

This private two-day experience combines a rainforest hike on Kilimanjaro with a day in the Chagga foothills, with a licensed mountain guide.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 2 days
• Start and end: your hotel in Moshi or Arusha
• Type: private tour with licensed mountain guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; a hike of about 16 kilometres with 900 metres of ascent on day 1

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Marangu route rainforest.
• Mandara Hut and the Maundi Crater.
• Materuni village.
• The Materuni waterfall.

WHY THIS WORKS
You experience Kilimanjaro without a week-long climb, at a pace and with a guide chosen for you.

WHO IT SUITS
Walkers, nature lovers and travellers combining safari and beach.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
To reach the summit, ask us for a 6- to 8-day climb on the Machame or Lemosho route.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The forest is often wet and muddy; bring a rain jacket and good boots. Kilimanjaro National Park fees are high and are included.

days.name: A rainforest hike on Kilimanjaro to Mandara Hut and the Maundi Crater
days.description:
What to expect: the lower slopes of Kilimanjaro.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 7:30 and drive to the Marangu Gate at 1,860 metres. You hike up through the montane rainforest, among giant ferns, moss-draped trees and wild orchids, where black-and-white colobus monkeys leap through the canopy. After about three hours you reach Mandara Hut, at 2,720 metres, where climbers spend their first night. After a packed lunch, a short trail leads to the rim of the Maundi Crater, from which, on clear days, you see Kibo, the snowy summit, and the plains of Kenya. You walk back down to the gate and return to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up.
08:30 – Marangu Gate.
09:00 – Hike through the rainforest.
12:00 – Mandara Hut and lunch.
13:00 – Maundi Crater.
14:00 – Descent.
16:30 – Back at the gate.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Clouds often cover the summit by midday.

INCLUDED: vehicle, guide, park fees, packed lunch.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

days.name: Materuni waterfall and a Chagga coffee experience
days.description:
What to expect: the Chagga foothills.

Your guide takes you to Materuni, a Chagga village in the foothills. You walk through banana groves and coffee plants to the Materuni waterfall, which drops about 80 metres into a pool where you can swim. Back in the village, a Chagga family shows you how coffee is grown, harvested, roasted over a fire and ground in a wooden mortar to a song, and you drink the result. Lunch is Chagga food, with a taste of mbege banana beer, before you return to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Pick-up.
10:00 – Walk to the Materuni waterfall.
12:00 – Coffee experience.
13:00 – Chagga lunch.
15:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Bring swimwear for the waterfall pool, which is cold.

INCLUDED: vehicle, guide, entrance, coffee experience, lunch.
NOT INCLUDED: tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability, hotels and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How fit do we need to be?
faq.answer: Reasonably fit: day 1 is a hike of about 16 kilometres with 900 metres of climbing.

faq.question: Will we see the summit?
faq.answer: On clear mornings, from the Maundi Crater; clouds often gather by midday.

faq.question: Will we get altitude sickness?
faq.answer: Unlikely at 2,720 metres, but go slowly and drink water.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Day 2 suits all ages; day 1 suits older children used to hiking.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Day 1 is not; day 2 involves a steep path to the waterfall.

faq.question: Can we climb to the summit?
faq.answer: Yes, on a 6- to 8-day climb, which we can arrange.

faq.question: Can we do only one of the days?
faq.answer: Yes, each day can be booked separately on request.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Hiking boots, a rain jacket, layers and swimwear for the waterfall.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: June to October and January to February; April and May are very wet.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary on safari in Tanzania: guides, drivers and camp staff appreciate a tip if you were happy with their service, but it is always your choice. Your guide can suggest typical amounts.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
